exit_state: Product compatibility, component capacity, quality, commitments and continuing service rights explain why equal financial totals can conceal different feasible operations. The connected answer preserves reported statements and conditional histories separately. Two matched annual histories produce different operating/investing settlement pairs and payment timing; source-view and navigation correction consequences continue on the next page.
findings: The product-transition passage does not equate a successful launch with higher margin. Compatibility, inventory cohorts and contract dates give the operational history concrete content.

Supply agreements, supplier count, component yield, assembly and shipment remain different premises. The quality example separates inventory write-down, cancellation obligation, asset impairment and supplier reimbursement.
Service continuation adds dated content/software rights, developer response and payment/data permissions. Identical physical capacity permits different offerings when a right expires.
The connected Apple result explains the narrow meaning of completed statement-token queries and partial history reconstruction. Source dashes and unmatched cash populations remain visible.

The two liability histories preserve branch and period dependence. The alpha allocation is a presentation assumption, not a probability; combining marginal minima would create an impossible total. No new confirmed defect.
